hypotheses.title: Cluster name lookups (Domain Name System, DNS) fail: CoreDNS is failing in prod-eu-central
hypotheses.summary: Services in prod-eu-central cannot resolve names (8 services affected). CoreDNS is itself failing after its configuration changed, so every call that needs a lookup fails or times out.

evidence.text: Name lookups fail in 8 services (payments-api, notification-worker, cart-api, checkout-api, storefront, catalog-api, …), 38 errors, first at 19:05:31 UTC: "…— dial tcp: lookup api.payments-gw.example.net on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving".
The CoreDNS configuration changed: ConfigMap coredns Corefile: forward . /etc/resolv.conf { → forward . 10.20.0.53 10.20.0.54 {.
CoreDNS itself is failing (killed for running out of memory, failing name lookups, crash-looping, timing out; 22 signals).
Lookups also fail from notification-worker at 19:06:48 UTC: "…getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN smtp-relay.example.net".
CoreDNS pods are killed for running out of memory 8 times, so lookups time out while they restart.

hypotheses.title: coredns is running out of memory
hypotheses.summary: coredns in prod-eu-central keeps exceeding its memory limit and is killed for running out of memory (OOMKilled), then restarted.

evidence.text: coredns containers were killed for running out of memory (OOMKilled, 8 records from Kubernetes and the kernel, first at 19:09:37 UTC), 6 restarts so far.
Kubernetes reports CrashLoopBackOff for coredns 7 times — the kill-restart cycle after each out-of-memory kill.
The kernel's out-of-memory killer on 2 nodes killed the coredns process 6 times.

rollbacks.title: Roll back Helm release coredns to r13 in prod-eu-central
commands: kubectl --context prod-eu-central -n kube-system rollout status deployment/coredns --timeout=5m
caveats: Helm records the rollback as a new revision (r15) with the contents of r13; r14 stays in the history.
It reverts all of r14's template changes, not only the suspect one: ConfigMap coredns Corefile: forward . /etc/resolv.conf { → forward . 10.20.0.53 10.20.0.54 {; coredns image tag 1.12.1 → 1.12.3.
If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease coredns -n kube-system), or it will re-apply r14 within minutes.
prerequisites: Access to kube-context prod-eu-central with rights to change namespace kube-system.
Check that r13 ran without problems before r14: helm history coredns -n kube-system --kube-context prod-eu-central --max 5

rollbacks.title: Restore ConfigMap coredns from r13
commands: helm get manifest coredns --revision 13 -n kube-system --kube-context prod-eu-central | yq 'select(.kind == "ConfigMap" and .metadata.name == "coredns")' | kubectl --context prod-eu-central -n kube-system apply -f -
kubectl --context prod-eu-central -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
caveats: Pods read ConfigMap values given as environment variables only at start-up, hence the restart; mounted files update after the kubelet sync (often a minute or more).
If the Corefile uses the reload plugin, CoreDNS also picks up the restored file once the kubelet syncs it; the restart applies it at once and clears the crash loop.

The node names look like Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), where CoreDNS is a managed add-on: change it through the coredns-custom ConfigMap, because edits to the coredns ConfigMap and Deployment are reconciled away.
The next helm upgrade applies the new value again unless the chart values change too.

If Argo CD or Flux manages this release, pause auto-sync first (argocd app set <app> --sync-policy none, or flux suspend helmrelease coredns -n kube-system), or it will revert this change within minutes.
